articleTitle: Effect of genetic sectoring on vehicle routing problems with time windows
publicationTitle: [1993] Proceedings IEEE International Conference on Developing and Managing Intelligent System Projects
abstract: In vehicle routing problems with time windows (VRPTW), a set of vehicles with limited capacity and travel time, are to routed from a central depot to a set of geographically dispersed customers with known demands within specified time windows. The VRSPTW is an NP-hard problem. That is, the time taken to solve it optimally increases exponentially with respect to the size of the problem. Genetic sectoring is a partitioning method that uses a genetic algorithm to find feasible solutions for the VRPTW. The genetic sectoring method was tested on a standard set of VRPTW problems. The solutions obtained using genetic sectoring gave better solutions than known conventional methods. The authors carry out a statistical analysis of the solutions obtained using genetic sectoring, to ascertain the kind of problems in which it would be advantageous to use the genetic sectoring method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Employee skills analysis using a hybrid neural network and expert system
publicationTitle: [1993] Proceedings IEEE International Conference on Developing and Managing Intelligent System Projects
abstract: The integration of neural networks and expert systems creates the potential for systems that are more powerful than ones using either of the techniques alone. The project presented uses hybrid systems for analyzing corporate databases. In this amplification, a neural network is trained to recognize patterns of information in an employee database, and an expert system component combines those results with a rule-based analysis to recommend staffing for projects. Results are presented along with implementation details and recommendations for further work in this area.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Developing a knowledge-based system for product position advertising strategy formulation
publicationTitle: [1993] Proceedings IEEE International Conference on Developing and Managing Intelligent System Projects
abstract: The progress is reported of a research project designed to explore an answer to the question 'Can knowledge-based systems (KBS) assist in product advertising decisions?' For this study a user-developed KBS prototype, the Product Position Strategy Advisor, was developed to advise market planners about the optimum advertising for a product. The recommendation is based on two major factors: the purchase behavior of the target market and the product's points of differences (i.e. the consumers' perceptions of the product's and the company's strengths and weaknesses). The prototype, which is still evolving, is described. It is limited to positioning consumer products which are new to the firm and sold primarily in supermarkets.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: C-based software toolkit for developing expert systems
publicationTitle: [1993] Proceedings IEEE International Conference on Developing and Managing Intelligent System Projects
abstract: The Interactive Experimenter Planning System (IEPS) Group at AlliedSignal Technical Services Corp. has been developing expert systems for NASA-Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) since 1985. Several systems have been developed in the C language on IBM PCs and UNIX-based workstations. With the implementation of these systems, various generic, C-based tools for building new applications have been developed. These generic, C-based tools have now been organized into a toolkit called the IEPS Software Toolkit. The focus of this paper is on the IEPS Software Toolkit and its use. The categories of tools in the toolkit that are described include: data formatting and report generation tools, user interface tools, database tools, strategic planning tools and tactical planning tools.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Educating knowledge engineers on knowledge acquisition
publicationTitle: [1993] Proceedings IEEE International Conference on Developing and Managing Intelligent System Projects
abstract: Even though many universities are offering programs in knowledge engineering, it's a rarity that a course on knowledge acquisition is included in the knowledge engineering curriculum content. At George Washington University, a course on knowledge acquisition is required as part of the Master of Science program in Applied Artificial Intelligence and Expert Systems. This paper describes the need for more university courses on knowledge acquisition, which then can contribute to improving the state-of-the-art in expert systems development.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of a modular chip for a reconfigurable artificial neural network
publicationTitle: [1993] Proceedings IEEE International Conference on Developing and Managing Intelligent System Projects
abstract: This paper describes the design of the IBM fabricated basic neural unit (BNU) which can be used as a building block for a general-purpose reconfigurable artificial neural network (GRANNet). As a first step, a fully reconfigurable 2-BNU VLSI circuit is designed, implemented and tested. The hardware and software requirements of this implementation are presented. This paper also examines the issue of topological reconfigurability.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The design of an ITS dedicated to industrial proceedings
publicationTitle: [1993] Proceedings IEEE International Conference on Developing and Managing Intelligent System Projects
abstract: In industry, engineers have to apply their knowledge and understanding to real problems. They need to develop a qualitative understanding of how industrial systems work. The authors discuss the possibility of integrating simulation and artificial intelligence techniques in industry and particularly in educational applications. Then they describe an architecture of an industrial educational system taking into account both simulation and artificial intelligence. In this context, the industrial proceeding is decomposed in basic phases; and small comprehensive elements (knowledge elements) are defined. Many lessons (dialogues) and educational tools are integrated. The tutor chooses admissible lessons and filters only one among them to be proposed to the student eliminating the ones which deviate from the educational strategy.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: ProloGA: a Prolog implementation of a genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: [1993] Proceedings IEEE International Conference on Developing and Managing Intelligent System Projects
abstract: This paper describes ProloGA, a Prolog implementation of a genetic algorithm. Chromosomes and associated parameters were stored in a Prolog database. The genetic operators of crossover, mutation, and population fitness were encoded in Prolog clauses. The test application demonstrated the feasibility of developing genetic algorithms in Prolog. The advantages of Prolog over conventional languages include database functionality, built-in 'don't care' operator, compact, declarative code, and use of heuristic knowledge. It is suggested that genetic algorithms may enhance Prolog applications by adding flexibility and adaptive rule discovery to the heuristic knowledge approach of Prolog. The combination may prove to be synergistic when applied to combinatorially large, complex, fuzzy problems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An adaptive function identification system
publicationTitle: [1993] Proceedings IEEE International Conference on Developing and Managing Intelligent System Projects
abstract: Given data in the form of a collection of (x,y) pairs of real numbers, the symbolic function identification problem is to find a functional model of the form y=f(x) that fits the data. This paper describes an adaptive system for solution of symbolic function identification problems that combines a genetic algorithm and the Levenberg-Marquardt nonlinear regression algorithm. The genetic algorithm uses an expression-tree representation rather than the more usual binary-string representation. Experiments were run with data generated using a wide variety of function models. The system was able to find a function model that closely approximated the data with a very high success rate.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Economic justification of intelligent system: a process approach
publicationTitle: [1993] Proceedings IEEE International Conference on Developing and Managing Intelligent System Projects
abstract: Although several methods for economic justification of general information system and office automation system are well documented, research on the feasibility of using these methods in justifying intelligent systems and on particular methods for intelligent system justification are very limited. This paper proposes a process approach to economic justification of intelligent system. As examples of that process approach, a method based on queuing models for economic justification of intelligent system application in service delivery and an activity price model for justification of intelligent system application in managerial decision support are discussed in detail.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Getting started in artificial intelligence (AI)
publicationTitle: [1993] Proceedings IEEE International Conference on Developing and Managing Intelligent System Projects
abstract: Software developers and managers at corporations are presented with a guideline to introducing their organization to artificial intelligence technology. Specifically through the implementations of expert or knowledge base systems, an organization can, in a relatively short period of time start taking advantage of AI technology. The author explores such areas as finding the right application, building a development team, selecting hardware and software and selecting training and consulting services, all aimed at quickly establishing an organization's AI capabilities.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Integrating rules into an object-oriented environment for process planning
publicationTitle: [1993] Proceedings IEEE International Conference on Developing and Managing Intelligent System Projects
abstract: Computer-aided process planning (CAPP) serves as a link in an integrated CAD/CAM system. The prototype system object-oriented computer aided process planning (OOCAP) presented in this paper is an object-oriented approach. The integration of rules, facts and operations in objects is the key concept in the system, as this makes the design process less procedural. The mechanism of triggering knowledge rules automatically is also described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A neural network approach to represent raster images by 3-order polynomials
publicationTitle: [1993] Proceedings IEEE International Conference on Developing and Managing Intelligent System Projects
abstract: Several approaches have been proposed to transform raster image into vectors. The authors propose a method which uses the characteristics of neural networks and monotonic concave functions to select the optimal windows and control points, then they use the method proposed by T. S. Tsui et. al. (1992) to transform a raster image into vectors. Experiments show that this neural network approach is robust in the presence of noise.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: ERDA: a user-centered, intelligent tutorial system for educational research in data abstractions
publicationTitle: [1993] Proceedings IEEE International Conference on Developing and Managing Intelligent System Projects
abstract: Educational Research in Data Abstractions (ERDA) is an intelligent tutorial system. The system's focus is to present animated and graphical representations of data abstractions and algorithms to supplement CS2 lectures. The authors deal with the research subjects of ERDA which include the following topics: a user-centered, highly portable interface that provides the user with a persistent framework and the ability to initiate nonlinear exploration; object-oriented lesson development techniques; standardization and documentation of lesson features that provides consistency and ensures future portability; and emphasis on interactive, user-directed learning.

articleTitle: From databases to rule bases
publicationTitle: [1993] Proceedings IEEE International Conference on Developing and Managing Intelligent System Projects
abstract: Induction is the process of reasoning from specific instances to general concepts. It is the development of universal concepts from individual episodes. Induction is used to develop rules of thumb (i.e. universal concepts) from databases (i.e. collections of records of individual episodes). In the expert system domain, induction is the ability to develop expert system rules from database records. If one was to look at a particular vendor offering induction, it could be looked upon as the ability to develop LEVEL5 or LEVEL5 OBJECT knowledge bases from FOCUS databases.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Managing intelligent systems with a deductive database: a first step towards federated knowledge based-systems
publicationTitle: [1993] Proceedings IEEE International Conference on Developing and Managing Intelligent System Projects
abstract: The work presented is part of a more important project which aims at designing federated knowledge based-systems (FKBS). The purpose of FKBSs is to make autonomous, heterogeneous and eventually geographically distributed KBSs cooperate with each other. The first step towards such systems consists in facilitating the designer's access to the pre-existing expert processing capabilities of the organization. In that regard, the purpose of the authors is to propose a deductive database (DDB) which one can record, structure, maintain and produce information about the existing KBS and their reusable components (knowledge base, control process etc.). In addition to intelligent system projects support, the DDB can also serve for knowledge communication, human training and software re-usability purposes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Developing an expert system to diagnose computer program outputs
publicationTitle: [1993] Proceedings IEEE International Conference on Developing and Managing Intelligent System Projects
abstract: Reported by the author is an expert system which enhances the capability of a nonlinear optimization program. Included are discussions on the knowledge acquisition aspect and the advantageous use of neural networks to accomplish knowledge acquisition. The expert system diagnoses the output of the NPSOL optimization package and seeks to find errors in the user-supplied inputs. These errors result from poor modeling formulation of the problem and poor parameter settings when running the program. A prototype system is installed on a Unix machine.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The key issue in reducing risk of liability with expert systems: product or service
publicationTitle: [1993] Proceedings IEEE International Conference on Developing and Managing Intelligent System Projects
abstract: Depending on the specific expert system application, individuals and organizations involved in the expert system development and marketing chain may unwittingly surrender themselves to high-risk exposure to tort liability legal actions, in the event that an innocent third party should suffer physical harm. The degree of risk turns on whether the expert system is viewed by the court as a 'product' or as a 'service'. The author examines the implication of this determination in two areas of tort, product liability and negligence, and then outlines the issues surrounding the 'product-service continuum' as applied specifically to the expert system development and marketing environment. Finally, the author presents proactive measures that expert system developers and vendors should consider in order to minimize exposure to risk.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Eliciting potential expert systems projects
publicationTitle: [1993] Proceedings IEEE International Conference on Developing and Managing Intelligent System Projects
abstract: This paper describes the methodology and how the authors developed it for eliciting potential expert system projects at the Internal Revenue Service (IRS). They intertwined demonstrations of existing IRS expert systems and examples from non-IRS applications with questions like 'Do you have anything like this?' to stimulate ideas of similar tasks that might be amenable to solution via an expert system. They also interspersed minitalks on artificial intelligence (AI) terminology at the appropriate level when they felt that such use could not be avoided. The result in one division of the IRS was over 20 potential future expert systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A model for estimating the cost of AI software development: what to do if there are no lines of code?
publicationTitle: [1993] Proceedings IEEE International Conference on Developing and Managing Intelligent System Projects
abstract: Since AI software development is becoming a common enterprise, requirements for cost estimation increase. Four traditional software cost models are examined for useful characteristics. After extending the function points model to expert systems, features of traditional software cost models are incorporated in a new model. The new model is designed so that it can be applied to costing expert systems, extended for other areas of AI, and used for costing traditional software development. Trial data are applied to the several models to give some understanding of the models' features.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A signature file method for Korean text retrieval
publicationTitle: [1993] Proceedings IEEE International Conference on Developing and Managing Intelligent System Projects
abstract: Many content-based retrieval methods for text have been proposed. Among them, signature file methods are useful when inverted files are not available. However, traditional word-oriented signature file methods cannot retrieve all the relevant text items in the variable-spacing environment such as Korean text. The authors describe a spacing-tolerant Korean signature extraction method using 2-syllable patterns. With this method, all the relevant text items are retrieved. The advantages of this method are presented by mathematical analysis and experimental performance comparison with a word-oriented method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Generalizing the Dempster-Shafer rule of combination to Boolean algebras
publicationTitle: [1993] Proceedings IEEE International Conference on Developing and Managing Intelligent System Projects
abstract: The Dempster-Shafer (D-S) theory of evidence is a significant generalization of classical Bayesian statistics which has been found to be promising for a variety of inexact reasoning applications. A number of substantial advances in the theory have been made, but no previous attempts have been made to generalize the theory to problem spaces which are not just the power sets of finite sets, which the original D-S theory addresses, but any kind of Boolean algebras. Included in this are spaces which are composed of propositions, and spaces which can be infinite. The authors generalize the theory by reworking some of the conventional D-S theorems and establish the relationships between 'weaker' forms of the familiar evidential functions. Although these relationships are not so strong as for finite sets, they show how they collapse to those stronger relations. Of particular interest is the orthogonal sum operation, and the authors generalize it so that it applies to any Boolean algebra. The potential advantages of this generalization in evidential reasoning application is discussed with the aid of a case study involving the 'Hominids of Turkana' (A. Walker, R.E.F. Leakey, 1978).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: FORM: a formal object-oriented requirements model based upon conceptual graphs
publicationTitle: [1993] Proceedings IEEE International Conference on Developing and Managing Intelligent System Projects
abstract: Information system requirements analysis can be viewed as a systematic process of modelling the problem domain. A model is constructed during this process which reflects human understanding of the domain. The authors introduce the FORM requirements model (formal object-oriented requirements model) based on conceptual graphs, whose graphical and linear representations provide a simple unifying formalism for the main concepts of requirements modelling based upon the object-oriented paradigm. An object class in FORM is a description of attributes, associations, and events. Actors are attached to event descriptions so that the procedural knowledge of events can be described. FORM has precise semantics and a set of formal model primitives which provide a means to model problem domains at the conceptual level with a formal basis.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Applying constraint propagation technology to an expert system planning Hubble Space Telescope observations
publicationTitle: [1993] Proceedings IEEE International Conference on Developing and Managing Intelligent System Projects
abstract: A relatively simple yet powerful way to represent temporal constraints is as suitability functions, which identify intervals during which a constraint allows or precludes a given activity. The authors describe the successful application of this framework to Transformation, an expert system for planning Hubble Space Telescope (HST) observations. TRANS is charged with many tasks requiring constraint checking, including ordering observations, grouping those performed together and determining timing links between them. These tasks have been successfully performed using the Micro-Spike package, which supports the generation, propagation and path consistency of temporal constraints.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: CMS: a knowledge-based tool for intelligent information systems application development
publicationTitle: [1993] Proceedings IEEE International Conference on Developing and Managing Intelligent System Projects
abstract: This paper describes the design and implementation of CMS, an intelligent knowledge-based tool to help organization members execute organizational procedures. CMS is aimed at automating the relationships and roles of organization members, rather than just transactions, so that a procedure can be executed by groups of problem solvers acting autonomously, cooperatively and collaboratively to achieve the collective goal. This collaborative process model supports the definition, execution, monitoring, and dynamic modification of organizational procedures, and is implemented as an object oriented knowledge-based system. The author's primary intent in this paper is to document the implementation strategy he employed, which is based on the integration of object-oriented programming within the logic programming environment of Prolog. This integration proved to be a powerful application development environment preserving the best features of both technologies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Automating knowledge acquisition for prototype reuse
publicationTitle: [1993] Proceedings IEEE International Conference on Developing and Managing Intelligent System Projects
abstract: This paper discusses the problem of automatically creating reusable software artifacts. A fundamental model for the structuring of reusable artifact libraries, the acquisition of reusable artifacts into libraries, and the location of reusable artifacts in libraries is described. A knowledge-based method for automatically generating reusable artifacts based on a domain knowledge base and consistent generalization is given. Tools based on this method and employed in the DProto system are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An incentive to build an intelligent system to cope with complexity derived from systems' interaction-through the case of water management
publicationTitle: [1993] Proceedings IEEE International Conference on Developing and Managing Intelligent System Projects
abstract: How can one identify the complexity of a system? Having identified it, how can one cope with it? Facing these heavy issues, the authors explain and sketch their thoughts by stating the necessity of building an intelligent system to enable them to solve or partly solve the problems by dealing with one aspect of the complexity-the part derived from systems' interaction. 'Coping with the complexity' then means to bring different levels of a systems' interaction onto one so called 'manageable level'. The authors propose the development of an intelligent system on the following levels: a functional level including a scope of its functions; a systematic level including a set of principles for its integration; a modelling level including an approach to model it.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of a system for accessing lessons learned
publicationTitle: [1993] Proceedings IEEE International Conference on Developing and Managing Intelligent System Projects
abstract: The development of a prototype system for accessing lessons learned to support military planning is described. The system accesses lessons learned, developed in various formats for a variety of automated systems, in the relevant planning context. The requirements-definition process, implementation, and observations on system development are discussed. Representation and indexing schemes for lessons learned are described. Although primarily used in defense-related areas, the lessons-learned system is also applicable to nondefense areas (e.g., environmental management, energy facility operation).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Learning IS active: an intelligent social learning system
publicationTitle: [1993] Proceedings IEEE International Conference on Developing and Managing Intelligent System Projects
abstract: This paper describes the design framework and some development issues of the project, LISA (learning IS active), which uses a network of computers to teach freshmen for the course 'Introduction to Computer Science'. The research is inter-disciplinary in nature, comprising computing, multimedia, artificial intelligence, cognitive science, computer network, etc. For example, different medium information provides multiple learning cues for the students while techniques of artificial intelligence allow the system to better adapt to individual student's needs. A novel element of this research is to engender student's initiatives or motives to learn by engaging the student in a learning environment with rich social context. Some pilot studies of the project have been conducted.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A biological-based neural network model of leech reflexive behaviors
publicationTitle: [1993] Proceedings IEEE International Conference on Developing and Managing Intelligent System Projects
abstract: An artificial neural network is built and trained to model the local bending reflex of the leech Hirudo Medicinalis. The model is validated by the data provided from physiological experiments. The training data and topology of the neural network is based on data gathered from physiological experiments. A graphical representation of the leech is constructed as a high level interface to the artificial neural network. This interface is used to determine the appropriateness of responses to different stimulus patterns. The artificial neural network is tested to see if it can generalize its repertoire of behaviors to untrained stimulus patterns. The leech provides the authors with a simple neurostructure that can be understood with today's technologies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A knowledge based object-oriented database schema generator
publicationTitle: [1993] Proceedings IEEE International Conference on Developing and Managing Intelligent System Projects
abstract: The design and implementation are discussed of a knowledge based object-oriented database (OODB) schema generator called KERO. KERO converts entity-relationship (ER) diagrams into structurally object-oriented database schema. A set of rules translating ER schema to OODB schema and their implementation are discussed with examples. KERO's input ER schema are capable of containing most of the semantic constructs used in the literature. The ER approach has been the most popular methodology for the relational database design. KERO allows one to utilize in the design of OODB schema the valuable knowledge of information engineers, as obtained through the design and use of relational database systems using the ER methodology. The KERO system has been implemented in MIKE, which is a meta-interpreter written in Prolog.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: IEEE International Conference on Developing and Managing Intelligent System Projects
publicationTitle: [1993] Proceedings IEEE International Conference on Developing and Managing Intelligent System Projects
